\chapter{Dijo Que --- Both Verbs Step Back}
\label{ch:dijo-que}
\hlchaptermodality{213}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can report what someone said, with the tense the report actually needs.}

I can report what someone said, with the tense the report actually needs.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[dijo que]{dijo que}

\label{lesson:ES-C57-dijo-que}



\begin{quote}
Report it in the present. (\emph{Dice que está cansado}.)

Now move only the first verb into the past. (\emph{Dijo}...)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: both verbs move}]
\begin{quote}
\emph{\textbf{Dice}} \emph{que} \emph{\textbf{está}} \emph{cansado.} \emph{\textbf{Dijo}} \emph{que} \emph{\textbf{estaba}} \emph{cansado.}
\end{quote}

The inner sentence cannot stay in the present once the reporting has moved back. It steps back too — into the \textbf{imperfect}.

Two more, so the shape is unmistakable:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{now} & \textbf{reported later} \\
\midrule
\emph{Dice que trabaja.} & \emph{Dijo que} \emph{\textbf{trabajaba}}. \\
\emph{Dice que hace calor.} & \emph{Dijo que} \emph{\textbf{hacía}} \emph{calor.} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{culture}
Of the two pasts you own, why this one?

Because of what the imperfect was always for: \textbf{what was going on}, rather than what happened and finished. And that is precisely what a report describes. He was tired \emph{at the moment he spoke} — not for an instant, and with no news about when it started or stopped.

The preterite would say something else entirely. It would package his tiredness as one completed event, which is not what he told you.

So the backshift is not a rule about reporting at all. It is the imperfect doing the job it has always done, in a place you had not needed it yet.
\end{culture}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Dijo que estaba cansado}
  \item the present version, then the reported one, back to back
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
When \emph{dice} becomes \emph{dijo}, what happens to the verb after \emph{que}? (It moves into the \textbf{imperfect}.)

And why that past and not the other one? (Because the report is about \textbf{what was going on} when he spoke.)
\end{tcolorbox}
